comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 programme-specific regulations and cohort page control the standard 180 EC full-time Philosophy bachelor, taught in Dutch with some English. The major comprises 60 EC of first-year courses, 30 EC in one advanced package, 15 EC of disciplinary breadth, a 7.5 EC preparation seminar and a 7.5 EC thesis. The remaining 60 EC includes a coherent 30 EC package and 30 EC of open choices, with at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3. The four advanced package courses plus seminar and thesis satisfy the 45 EC level-3 major minimum. The 2026 cohort is expected to take the odd-year History of Political Philosophy when it reaches the advanced package in 2027–28, based on the published alternation. The current cohort page and regulations take precedence over the recruitment page’s bridging-package description.

components.name: History of Political Philosophy (FI3V19001)
components.note: This course alternates with History of Ethics. Utrecht lists History of Political Philosophy for academic years starting in an odd calendar year, which includes 2027–28.

components.name: Philosophy of Philosophy (FI3V19018)
components.note: Students complete at least 22.5 EC at level 3 before beginning the graduation sequence. The seminar prepares the thesis in the following block.

components.name: Bachelor Thesis Philosophy (FI3V19053)
components.note: This example uses the 7.5 EC thesis. The 15 EC research project requires agreement with the programme coordinator and uses 7.5 EC of open elective space.

components.name: Coherent elective package
components.note: Choose a minor, a second Philosophy specialisation or approved study abroad. Across all 60 EC of elective space, at least 15 EC must be at level 2 or 3.

components.name: Open electives
components.note: Choose electives, a second minor or an internship of up to 15 EC.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The EER requires one of three 30-EC deepening packages and lists Ethics and Politics first. No target-specific evidence distinguishes a student's choice, so the first-listed package is used as a neutral tie-break before any UCR comparison. This route choice instantiates the comparator only; all three official directions remain separately assessed as programme-interest candidates.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match covers the broad cross-subdisciplinary Philosophy core. The first two official deepening-package directions, Ethics and Politics and Language, Mind and World, each produce a coherent and materially distinct 24-course UCR curriculum and are included as alternatives 2 and 3. The remaining official What Is the Human Being? direction is independently coherent and supported by philosophical anthropology, continental philosophy and identity interests, but the production contract permits at most three UCR alternatives; it is therefore recorded as maximum-reached rather than mischaracterised as incoherent or infeasible.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Philosophy bachelor studies questions about knowledge, reality, moral responsibility and political justice. Students develop philosophical arguments, read texts from different periods and choose an advanced package. This example follows Ethics and Politics.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options share study of ethics and the philosophy of mind. They differ in their emphasis on historical interpretation, rights and public institutions, or cognition and AI. Utrecht offers a more extensive philosophy curriculum and requires a philosophy thesis.
